app.title: Last Combustion
app.tagline: Racing team simulation game based in a post-petrol world, where the last petrolheads ply their craft.
consent.title: Usage statistics
consent.body: This site can send anonymous usage statistics to GameAnalytics and Google Analytics: which screens and actions are used, how seasons go and how money moves. It never sends names, your garage or your saves. Nothing is sent or stored unless you accept, and you can change your mind at any time.

starter.intro: Pick one car and one driver to start with. The cars and drivers you pass on go on the market and to free agency.

supply.explain: Every round the garage pays for electricity, water, race fuel, road fuel and haulage. Without a contract it pays the market rate; a contract fixes the price for its length, at a discount the supplier agrees to.
supply.saving: Your Operations Director takes {percent}% off every bill.
supply.spot: Spot market: you pay {rate}% of the base price.
supply.contract: Contract with {name}: {discount}% off, you pay {rate}% of the base price until {year}.
supply.ineligible: Needs prestige {prestige}, or does not serve your region.
supply.negotiating: Negotiating with {name} for {category}. A fair discount is about {fair}%. Patience {patience}.
supply.counter: They counter: {discount}% off for {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}.
supply.walked: {name} walks away and will not talk again this year.
upgrades.intro: Parts change power, weight, grip and how much of the road-legality budget is left. A car over budget fails scrutineering.
plate.label: Licence plate {plate}, {state}

upgrades.serviceNone: Parts are as good as new
drivers.intro: Drivers without a seat this season. Negotiate a contract, then put the driver in your entry before the season starts.
drivers.trainingIntro: Training speeds a driver's improvement, slows their decline and lets them climb a little past their potential. It is paid for at the end of the season, and a garage that cannot pay gives none.
drivers.gearIntro: Gear wears with racing and gives less of its boost as it does. Worn pieces also stop counting towards a supplier set.
drivers.stats: Rating {rating}. Pace {pace}, consistency {consistency}, racecraft {racecraft}, tyres {tyres}, composure {composure}, wet {wet}.
drivers.negotiating: Negotiating with {name}. A fair salary is around {fair} a year. Patience: {patience}.
drivers.counter: They counter: {salary} a year for {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}, with the garage keeping {share}% of the prize money.
drivers.walked: {name} has walked away and will not talk again this year.
sponsors.intro: A title sponsor pays the garage a season fee, a sixth of it after each round. Bigger sponsors want a more famous garage.
sponsors.title: Title sponsor
sponsors.noDeal: The garage has no title sponsor.
sponsors.noneApproachable: No sponsor will talk to a garage of this standing yet.
sponsors.negotiating: Negotiating with {name}. A fair season fee is around {fair}. Patience: {patience}.
sponsors.counter: They counter: {fee} a season for {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}.
sponsors.walked: {name} has walked away and will not talk again this year.
money.intro: What the garage holds, and where it came from and went.
money.empty: Nothing has been paid or received yet.
entries.title: Entries
entries.intro: An entry is one car and one driver. Each extra entry costs up to about {cost} a round in fees, tyres, servicing and travel. Entries can be changed until the season starts.
entries.full: The garage has as many entries as it is allowed.
entries.needCar: To add an entry you need a spare car that is not racing.
entries.needDriver: To add an entry you need a signed driver who is not racing. Sign one in the Drivers panel.
dealer.heading: Dealers
dealer.newIntro: Every model on sale this year, at the list price less any deal your garage has with the manufacturer.
dealer.sellIntro: A dealer pays a share of a car's value and lists it on the used market for more. A car with an entry this season cannot be sold.
dealer.nothingToSell: You have no car to sell that is not racing.
auction.heading: Auctions
auction.none: There is no auction open. The next one opens after the next round.
auction.intro: Name the most you will pay for a lot. The auction raises your bid only as far as it must to beat the others, so you pay one step over the second best bid, never more than your maximum. The buyer pays {premium}% on top and a seller loses {fee}%. The auction closes after the next round, and a lot under its reserve goes unsold.
auction.youPay: You would pay up to {total} with the premium
auction.nothingToConsign: You have no spare car to consign. A car with an entry this season cannot be sold.
auction.lastSummary: {sold} lots sold and {unsold} did not, for {turnover} in all.
auction.lastNothing: You did not buy, sell or bid on anything.
staff.intro: Mechanics look after the cars. A good crew saves wear on parts and the cost of crash repairs, and every mechanic is paid each round.
staff.explain: A full crew is one expert mechanic for each of your {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}: skill counts, so two average mechanics cover one expert. Notice costs a round's wages.
staff.none: You employ no mechanics, so the cars are looked after by the owner.
